items.title: Tutti fan' Drupal - Welcome to Drupal(Con)!
items.full_description:
Robert Douglass, jam

An opening session designed to prepare attendees for success at DrupalCon and within the Drupal community. The presenters deliver practical advice about Drupal, the conference experience, and thriving as a community member through musical performance, storytelling, humor, and guest appearances.

The duo has previously created themed musical performances at multiple DrupalCons, including Sound of Music adaptations and other creative productions. Dries Buytaert has praised their work, stating: "It's just hilarious. It's not a very technical session, but it is really, really awesome."

Key takeaways include:
- Tips for maximizing your DrupalCon experience
- Securing good seating for the keynote immediately following
- Community history and context

items.title: Driesnote
Drupal 8 for Site Builders
items.full_description:
"Dries' dream to eliminate the programmer comes closer with every new major release of Drupal. While we are not there yet, Drupal 8 has become more powerful and flexible out of the box for site builders."

The presentation explores major new capabilities available to site builders in Drupal 8, including Views integration, configurable fields such as entity reference and date types, multilingual enhancements, blocks and layouts functionality, and responsive image features with breakpoints. The talk emphasises how "Creating a site has just become easier for everyone."

items.title: Are GPL and Patents Limits or Opportunities to Grow Business?
items.full_description:
This session examines two critical intellectual property considerations in open source development: the GPL license and software patents. While often perceived as opposing forces, the talk explores their practical implications for software businesses within the Drupal community.

The presentation challenges polarized viewpoints by analyzing how GPL, though it "makes it difficult to create scalable software licensing business," can simultaneously enhance platform popularity and enable innovative business models. Similarly, patent considerations are reframed—third-party patents may create uncertainty, yet patent threats rarely impact smaller companies significantly. When strategically pursued, patents can provide competitive advantages and facilitate business growth.

items.title: Selenium/Webdriver: What, where, why and how
items.full_description:
Selenium has been discussed in Drupal communities as a tool for ensuring site features work across browsers and preventing regressions. This session addresses the practical challenges of implementation.

The speaker shares experience using Selenium in continuous integration environments at The Economist, having worked with the tool in both PHP and Java contexts against Drupal sites and general websites. While focusing primarily on Selenium, insights about scaling testing environments apply to other frameworks like Windmill.

Topics covered:
- Selenium and Webdriver fundamentals and selection criteria
- Making an API to help your Selenium framework (e.g. testdata module)
- Writing stable tests through patterns and Page Objects
- Scaling test suites using Selenium Grid and cloud servers
- Third-party tools and resources
- Migration from SeleniumRC to Webdriver

Intended for those with CI experience and basic Selenium knowledge.

items.title: D8 Lessons Learned and How We Can Make D9 Better
items.full_description:
A post-mortem examination of Drupal 8 core development from a project management perspective. The presenter shares lessons learned after over a year managing the project, including insights from fellow PMs and team retrospectives.

Key topics covered:
- Community challenges: lack of interest in project management, planning difficulties, and resource constraints
- Volunteer project obstacles: unreliable deadlines and unpredictability
- Core development issues: lack of visibility into issues, unpredictability and sheer size of the beast

The session proposes solutions for Drupal 9 development:
- Strategies for encouraging adoption of new releases
- Team organization approaches to support core development
- Resource requirements for building sustainable teams

An updated version from a Portland presentation, featuring new theories and ideas, with Q&A for community brainstorming.

items.title: Drupal 8 Ready
items.full_description:
This session examines the core competencies required for Drupal 8 readiness across multiple roles. "Drupal 8 may be the biggest change in Drupal's history," with substantial portions of core functionality being replaced by enhanced systems.

The presentation covers significant shifts including the introduction of the Plugin system for developers, Twig templating for front-end work, and new approaches to responsive, accessible, and mobile-friendly development.

Rather than providing technical specifics, the session offers "a comprehensive and concise introduction to Drupal 8," addressing needs for developers, project managers, system administrators, and content managers. It outlines essential skills and practical preparation strategies for the upcoming release.

items.title: Escaping From Alcatraz - Migration
items.full_description:
Have you ever tried to migrate your site from one framework to another? Have you ever tried to upgrade your Drupal core from older to newer system? Have you ever come to conclusion that there are less successful implementations?

Platform migration and data transfer represent ongoing challenges for technical implementers. The presenters share experience from "massive and sophisticated migration projects," focusing on various examples of migrating from diverse sources to Drupal.

The session offers "a survival kit and action plan to get prepared for your escape from 'Alcatraz'" and guidance on getting projects safely completed.

items.title: Tag, You're It! Keep Your Reverse-Proxy Cache Up-to-Date
items.full_description:
This presentation addresses the challenge of keeping reverse-proxy caches current in production environments. While Varnish, Squid, or Nginx accelerate Drupal sites, outdated content often persists despite using Expire and Purge modules.

Columbia Law School developed a cache tagging approach to maximise Varnish performance while ensuring fresh content delivery. The session covers:

- Current cache invalidation limitations and why they sometimes fail
- Emerging smart cache developments in Drupal 8 and Varnish Cache Tagging
- HTTP Cache Tag Auto module — a Drupal 7 solution supporting automatic tagging based on entities, menu items, themes, blocks, taxonomy terms, and views
- Rules integration
- Hooks for module extensibility
- Sample reverse-proxy configuration files

items.title: From Home Page to Hypertext Preprocessor and back again
items.full_description:
This presentation explores the origins of PHP while advocating for a return to personalised web experiences. The speaker proposes examining how technological innovation often overshadows "social and political consequences" of digital work.

A three-step method is presented for creating truly personal home pages across devices, addressing needs of end users, administrators, and content providers alike. The core argument emphasises that "we must work to put non-developers back into the equation and thus make Drupal even stronger," ultimately strengthening community engagement beyond purely technical advancement.

items.title: Everything is Commerce: Beyond the Shopping Cart
items.full_description:
rszrama, Damien Tournoud
Commerce Guys

"We're not just talking about a shopping cart any more...Commerce is broader than you think. It's transactions. Information. Connection."

The session explores how Drupal Commerce extends beyond ecommerce to encompass broader site interactions. Participants will learn how commerce principles apply across government, education, and other sectors where "the exchange of ideas is just as important as the exchange of money."

Commerce Guys presents their toolkit — including Commerce Kickstart, Commerce Marketplace, Commerce Platform, and Commerce Mobile — demonstrating how Drupal Commerce serves as "a competitive framework for high profile eCommerce projects" and helps organisations win significant ecommerce contracts.

items.title: Drupal.org Content Working Group: community conversation
items.full_description: The Drupal.org Content Working Group hosts an open community conversation about governance and development of Drupal.org. Participants will learn about current initiatives and future plans, including landing pages projects, user research, persona development, and content strategy. The session invites attendees to share their feedback on desired content improvements for the platform.

items.title: Your first Drupal 8 module (Lab)
items.full_description:
Drupal 8 represents a fundamental shift in module development methodology. Rather than relying on traditional hook-based approaches, the new system emphasises "a careful construction of services, plugins, controllers, and listeners." The platform prioritises object-oriented architecture over array-based structures.

This hands-on workshop guides developers through creating a Drupal 8 module while exploring the system's architectural foundations. Participants will engage in practical coding exercises throughout the session.

Key topics:
- Services (distinct from web services)
- State system functionality
- Plugin architecture and implementation
- Block development improvements
- Controllers and routing systems
- Event listeners
- Configuration management and deployment strategies
- Entity systems

Prerequisites: Attendees should bring a laptop with a functional development environment and a pre-installed Drupal 8 installation ready for use.

items.title: Performance Lab
items.full_description:
"Did you ever experience a slow Drupal site or are you annoyed by the fact that your awesome site is too slow to really enjoy it?" This hands-on lab examines Drupal performance bottlenecks and optimisation strategies.

The session consists of two parts: an initial presentation covering performance fundamentals (45 minutes), followed by real-world site optimisation work with attendees (90 minutes), plus short breaks.

Topics covered include identifying performance issues through queries, entities, and field rendering; implementing caching strategies via pages, blocks, and Ctools; utilising optimisation modules like Memcache and Entity Cache; configuring Varnish; and profiling tools such as XhProf and NewRelic.

Participants are encouraged to bring development environments of their own projects for analysis and optimisation during the session.

items.title: From Not-Invented-Here to Proudly-Found-Elsewhere: A Drupal 8 Story
items.full_description:
Drupal has traditionally operated independently, but Drupal 8 marked a significant shift toward integrating external code. The platform now leverages components from the broader PHP ecosystem, including Symfony's HTTP Foundation, Doctrine, Guzzle, Twig, Assetic, and EasyRDF, unified through PSR-0 and Composer standards.

This session explores how Drupal transitioned from "Not-Invented-Here" to "Proudly-Found-Elsewhere," examining the challenges of this architectural change and the opportunities it creates. The presentation covers why this shift matters for developers and how "Drupal's enormous talent pool has been made even larger" through active contribution to the wider PHP community.

items.title: Multilingual site tools in Drupal 8
items.full_description:
Drupal 8 fundamentally changes how language is understood on sites. This session covers installation, language settings, content language and translation support, software translation, and configuration language.

"Drupal 8 aims to provide a familiar environment yet it has many fundamental underlying changes in terms of how it understands language on your site."

The presentation explores new features for both single foreign language and multilingual sites. It's designed for those with Drupal 6 or 7 multilingual building experience seeking Drupal 8 capabilities, though beginners will also benefit from the content.

items.title: Drupal Fixed Budget Projects: The Art of Estimates
items.full_description:
This session addresses the challenge of bidding on fixed-budget Drupal projects when RFPs often lack sufficient detail. The presenter shares Adyax's approach to ensuring project delivery and profitability.

Key topics covered include:
- How to analyse an RFP and convert it to a Drupal Project Plan
- Calculating template costs and related expenses
- Identifying unclear feature descriptions in RFPs
- Competitive pricing strategies through options
- Estimation methodologies and planning techniques
- Risk assessment for margin protection
- Drupal's distinct advantages versus other CMS/frameworks
- Margin monitoring throughout project execution
- Managing change requests and client expectations
- Common Drupal shop mistakes to avoid

The session incorporates concrete examples throughout.

items.title: Automated Acceptance Tests with Behat
items.full_description:
This session explores Behavioural Driven Development (BDD) using Behat, a tool that enables developers to deliver applications matching stakeholder intentions. The presentation covers agile project development challenges, testing benefits for confident delivery, prioritising test coverage, and justifying testing investments.

Key topics include:
- Agile development principles and stakeholder alignment
- Testing's role in confident application delivery
- Test prioritisation strategies
- Building business cases for testing
- Test writing approaches
- Live demonstration of Behat in action

The session references Dan North's 2006 article introducing BDD as "not just a means to test our applications but to deliver applications that matter."

items.title: Introducing user-centered design in a 100,000+ person corporation
items.full_description:
A presenter with seven years of experience in the Drupal community shares insights on integrating user-centered design at a major global bank. The talk explores the challenge of "pushing innovation within a huge corporation" while transitioning from freelance work to enterprise environments.

Key topics include examining whether default interfaces genuinely serve users' needs, conducting behavioural research to enhance performance, and navigating organisational resistance. The speaker addresses the tension between a "success driven approach" focused on management objectives versus prioritising actual user requirements.

Attendees will learn practical research methodologies for implementing user-centered design across organisations, discover how these approaches can "increase conversion rate," and gain perspective on balancing business goals with genuine user needs in large-scale projects.

items.title: Double Session: Patch Reviews & Turning Regular People into Mentors
items.full_description:
Patch Reviews: Get good reviews, give good reviews. Faster.

The session addresses challenges in Drupal core development where over 2,000 core issues await review. Poor review quality and slow turnaround frustrate contributors and cause some to abandon efforts. The presenters discuss strategies for improving patch review workflows, including:
- How patch authors can request specific feedback types
- Tools for efficient review (dreditor, drush, simplytest.me)
- Best practices for informative reviews, such as numbered reproduction steps and browser compatibility notes
- Ways Drupal.org could better support these processes

Stories & strategies: turning regular people into mentors of mentors

This segment focuses on the Drupal Core Mentoring program, designed to grow the contributor base sustainably. Topics include practical mentoring techniques for welcoming newcomers, matching appropriate tasks, maintaining engagement during challenges, and helping mentees develop independence. The session serves mentors, potential mentors, and sprint organisers seeking to strengthen Drupal's contributor ecosystem.

items.title: High performance sites with Drupal and Cache Control module
items.full_description:
Janne Salo
Exove

Building high-performance Drupal sites is challenging, and internal caching often proves insufficient. This session explores external caching strategies, focusing on the Cache Control module that integrates Drupal with Varnish HTTP accelerator and other external HTTP caches.

The module enables caching for both anonymous and authenticated users. The presentation examines three real-world cases: a high-traffic site where administrators are the only authenticated users, demonstrating ideal Cache Control conditions; a site with mostly authenticated users generating substantial content and personalised content; and a geographically distributed site using Fastly CDN. Each case illustrates how Cache Control performed, the challenges encountered, and practical solutions implemented in demanding performance environments.

items.title: Evolving frontend development; dancing on the tip of a hurtling rocket
items.full_description:
Front end development constantly evolves with shifting tools, standards, and best practices. Since the iPhone's introduction, progressive enhancement, responsive design, HTML5, JavaScript frameworks, and mobile web access have transformed the landscape.

Drupal 7 produced HTML by default, but "Drupal 8 installation, we can now request JSON in addition to HTML." This architectural shift enables dynamic front end applications, though gaps remain — the entity CRUD API will be incomplete, requiring contrib developers to fill voids.

The session explores how Drupal supports complex front end architectures through:
- Decoupling front end templates from backend data using frameworks like Backbone.js
- Balancing single page application dynamism with RESTful, addressable content management
- Identifying Drupal 8 functionality gaps for modern web development
- Using tools to maintain pace with evolving front end practices

The discussion aims to help front end developers identify necessary Drupal features, understand their mechanisms, and write code effectively.

items.title: Universal Media Assets Management in Drupal with the Scald module
items.full_description:
This presentation celebrates the Scald module's CMSDay award for "Best Back-Office Innovation" and addresses the historical gap in Drupal's media management capabilities. The session covers:

- Evolution of media management in Drupal (versions 6–7)
- Core Scald concepts and architecture
- Media Library interface, WYSIWYG integration, and atom reference fields
- Supported media providers including videos, sounds, images, pdf, soundcloud, embed.ly, twitter, flickr, facebook, and commerce products
- Version 1.1 features: inline editing, cut/paste functionality, RTE contextualisation, custom players, responsive design, CKEditor integration, and multimedia galleries
- Real-world user implementations and feedback
- Future roadmap announcements

items.title: Drupal Chef: Bork Bork Bork!
items.full_description:
This presentation explores Chef, an open-source systems integration framework that helps reduce inconsistent server setups while enabling scalable, replicable architectures. The session demonstrates keeping development, staging, and production environments synchronised.

Beginning with fundamental LAMP stack concepts, the talk progresses through Drupal installation and Drush configuration. It then explores advanced tools including Jenkins, Behat, logging, and redundancy mechanisms to establish stable, reliable environments.

The presentation combines technical depth with humour throughout, making infrastructure automation accessible to developers new to Chef and configuration management practices.

items.title: Moving an Enterprise to Drupal: Setting Up Migration Projects for Success
items.full_description:
Chris Herring, Adam Asch, James Kutz
NBCUniversal

This session examines how NBCUniversal manages enterprise-level website migrations to a centralised Drupal platform across multiple brand divisions including Syfy, NBC.com, NBC News, Universal Studios, Bravo, Oxygen, and Telemundo.

The presenters discuss strategies for navigating "complex interactions with brand partners to ensure success," addressing methods to mitigate risk, empower development teams, and utilise Drupal community resources. Key focus areas include planning approaches and management techniques for coordinating migrations across a large enterprise with multiple stakeholders maintaining distinct brand identities.

items.title: Building Really Fast Websites with Drupal 8
items.full_description:
Drupal 8 delivers improved front-end performance by eliminating unnecessary JavaScript loads and implementing efficient entity caching to reduce HTML generation time. This accelerates page rendering on all devices, including mobile.

The framework addresses personalisation through client-side caching using localStorage/sessionStorage with intelligent cache invalidation, allowing "the same HTML (well, >90% the same — i.e. the most expensive parts)" to serve multiple users while maintaining individual customisation based on permissions and user interests.

Additionally, Drupal 8 introduces pluggable CSS and JavaScript optimisation, enabling custom minifiers and data-driven grouping strategies to achieve globally optimal asset bundling.

The session explores achieving comparable performance gains in Drupal 7 where applicable, focusing on delivering fast websites with strong perceived performance.

items.title: Assuring Quality on Drupal.org
items.full_description:
A team from the Git migration developed automated tests for Drupal.org using Behat and Mink, documenting over 675 scenarios. The presentation explores how Behaviour-Driven Development extends beyond test automation to encompass quality processes from the beginning.

The session examines three areas:

Past: Development history of the test suite, how tests are maintained, and analysis of decision-making and communication processes.

Present: Identifying strengths and critical improvement opportunities in current workflows.

Future: Learning how to contribute to ongoing efforts and identifying concrete next steps for improvements.

The core theme addresses "a graceful workflow where we develop the very best collaborative infrastructure we can while we continue to learn from and enjoy our labor."

items.title: The Pfizer Story: Building a Global Digital Marketing Platform with Drupal
items.full_description:
Mike Lamb, Director of Marketing Technology Strategy, Pfizer
Bryan House, VP of Product Marketing, Acquia

Managing individual sites presents challenges, but overseeing hundreds of digital marketing sites across 46 countries multiplies that complexity exponentially. Pfizer tackled this challenge by leveraging Drupal as the foundation of its solution.

The presentation examines how Pfizer addressed competing objectives: accelerating time-to-market while cutting costs. Rather than maintaining multiple separate codebases, the organisation built "a digital marketing platform for hundreds of sites on Drupal running on Acquia Cloud."

Mike Lamb discusses Drupal's role as the core of Pfizer's Digital Marketing platform, while he and Bryan House engage in a fireside chat-style Q&A addressing their practical experience implementing this enterprise-scale solution.

items.title: DevOps and Drupal in a large organisation: What we learned
items.full_description:
This session examines how a traditional media company with 60 years of history implemented DevOps practices to support continuous delivery of a high-traffic, multi-site Drupal installation managed by multiple large teams on a new Linux platform.

The presentation offers a candid, real-world perspective on introducing DevOps capabilities within an established organisation, rather than a startup environment. Attendees will learn both the successes and failures encountered during this transformation, gaining practical insights applicable to similar enterprise deployments.

items.title: Auditing Drupal sites
items.full_description:
Kalle Varisvirta, Technology Director at Exove

"We're doing a lot of audits for Drupal sites. What do we look for when doing an audit?" The presentation explores various perspectives on conducting Drupal audits, examining different purposes and providing case examples to help audiences understand the comprehensive scope of Drupal auditing work.

The session addresses why clients contract auditing services and how those motivations influence what auditors prioritise during evaluations. Attendees will learn what Drupal installations should address to successfully pass audits.

items.title: Using Backbone.js with Drupal 8 & 7
items.full_description:
Backbone.js is "a lightweight JavaScript framework which is freely based on MVC pattern" that enables developers to build single-page AJAX applications with minimal data transfer using REST approaches. The speaker, who authored a Backbone.js CookBook, explores JavaScript's role in Drupal and why this framework gained traction in major applications like Airbnb and Foursquare.

The session covers foundational concepts including similarities between Backbone and Drupal's architecture, familiarity with Underscore.js, and practical data-fetching techniques. Attendees learn how to implement the Backbone module within Drupal's ecosystem.

Advanced topics include the WSCCI initiative's implications and strategies for deeper Backbone integration within Drupal 8 core infrastructure.

items.title: Webform 4.0: Surveys in Drupal Improved
items.full_description:
The new Webform 4.0 offers features to make survey building and results collection better than ever. If you've been using Webform for a long time or just getting started with Drupal, come see the ways you can get the most out of Webform with the new version.

Topics covered:
- An introduction to the Webform UI
- Techniques for using tokens
- HTML formatting e-mails
- Sending e-mails to users based on selections
- Hiding and showing fields using conditionals
- Creating forms quickly with the Form Builder module
- Exporting your data to other programs
- Visualising data using charts and graphs

items.title: Taking the plunge ... becoming a contributor
items.full_description:
The presenter shares their personal journey transitioning from a Drupal user to an active community contributor. They describe "how I went from a simple consumer of Drupal to someone who participates and gives back code, time and bad jokes to the community."

The talk explores multiple pathways for getting involved, including creating contrib modules and themes, writing documentation, reviewing patches, hosting local meetup discussions, contributing to core, and mentoring others.

Drawing on two years of experience as an unofficial ambassador for new contributors in the New York Drupal meetup, this session aims to inspire attendees while providing actionable guidance for immediately beginning their own contribution journey.

items.title: Reinventing the Drupal design workflow
items.full_description:
The session explores how Drupal's development processes were designed by developers for developers, creating barriers for designers. The speakers note that "many of the tools and processes that designers commonly use to surface new ideas, critique each others work, arrive at consensus and measure success have no analogs at all on Drupal.org."

A key concern is that community recognition metrics are development-focused, measuring contributions like patches and modules rather than design work. The UX group debates two approaches: establishing a separate design-focused site or reforming the existing project module to better integrate design contributions.

The forum aims to discuss restructuring Drupal's development process to properly incorporate, recognise, and value design expertise alongside development contributions.

items.title: My Drupal project is rich: have fun and save money!
items.full_description:
VioMeneux
Actency

Over years in project management, two principles emerge: developers are always right, and project managers never walk alone. Success requires placing team members' profiles and skills at the heart of your process.

The session explores how to build the right team for your project — identifying who among Sitebuilders, Themers, Developers, Technical Project Managers, and Drupal Architects fits where. However, assembling talented people isn't enough; "Setting up a rugbymen team in the middle of the field might turn soon enough into a gigantic scrum mess, if you don't give each of them a clear scope."

Focusing on large project organisation and Drupal's suitability for such work, this presentation covers scopes, governance, and team member empowerment to create healthy, productive cycles where everyone thrives.

items.title: Beyond Style Guides: Building Responsive, Future Friendly Style Systems In Browser (Lab)
items.full_description:
This hands-on lab challenges the traditional approach to web design. The session argues that "Photoshop is not a web design tool" and that designing in-browser using modern development tools is essential for managing complexity in today's multi-device landscape.

Participants will explore Style Prototypes, learning how to build maintainable style systems leveraging Sass, Compass, JavaScript, Grunt, and Git. The workshop demonstrates how to integrate design-in-browser workflows into agile development processes for quick iteration and easy updates across sites.

Prerequisites: Attendees must be comfortable with Sass fundamentals, have the Style Prototype generator installed, be comfortable with command-line interfaces, and should have a GitHub account. This is a coding-intensive session requiring hands-on participation.

items.title: Fix me if you can (Lab)
items.full_description:
This session presents a real-world case study of diagnosing and fixing a severely broken Drupal site. Starting from a white screen of death, presenters guide the audience through identifying architectural issues, including poor module decisions, configuration problems, and code quality concerns.

The workshop covers "how the site is built and how is the balance made between contributed and custom modules," examining what commonly goes wrong across these layers. Participants learn to troubleshoot performance issues and security vulnerabilities through practical examples.

The presenters emphasise that "Drupal is a complex system" requiring understanding of all application layers. By working through real-world examples from large-scale Drupal websites, attendees gain exposure to debugging techniques and best practices across site architecture, code quality, and system administration — ultimately learning how to restore a compromised site to normal operation.

items.title: Twig and the new theme layer in Drupal 8
items.full_description:
Drupal 8 introduces a new template engine (Twig) and streamlined theme layer. The session covers the updated template syntax and addresses major challenges from Drupal 7 that have been resolved or are under development in Drupal 8.

Key improvement areas include:
- Syntax
- Consistency
- Complexity
- Redundancy
- Security

The presenters walk through changes to the theme layer, emphasising how Drupal 8 aims to be accessible for theme developers and newcomers while remaining logical for experienced professionals. The team seeks community input on ongoing refinements and invites participation in development efforts.

items.title: We need to teach people Drupal 8. Now
items.full_description:
Drupal 8's imminent release creates urgent need to train the community. The speaker, drawing on experience with training videos, workshops, and client training, proposes strategies to ease the learning curve.

Key proposals include:

1. Comparative learning: Provide "this is how it was in Drupal 7, and this is how it is now in Drupal 8" examples, allowing developers to build on existing knowledge rather than starting from scratch.

2. Teaching the "why": Beyond demonstrating implementation mechanics, explain the reasoning behind architectural decisions. Understanding why the Configuration Management Initiative exists and how it was designed helps developers apply tools to unforeseen problems.

3. Identifying obstacles: Address major learning hurdles specific to Drupal 8 so the community can develop targeted solutions.

The speaker emphasises that successful Drupal 8 adoption depends directly on effective community education and documentation.

items.title: Writing Unit Testable Code in Drupal 8
items.full_description:
As a developer, you want assurance that your code performs as intended across all scenarios and can be reliably reused in unforeseen contexts. Writing unit-testable code addresses both concerns simultaneously, since unit tests represent the first reuse of your class.

However, writing isolated unit tests becomes difficult when code has hard dependencies on its normal execution context. This session explores fundamentals of unit-testable code design, emphasising the Dependency Injection pattern for achieving loose coupling between classes. It examines how contributed modules from Drupal 7 can become unit-testable in Drupal 8 by adopting newly established best practices.

The presentation also covers essential techniques for writing PHPUnit tests for well-designed, loosely-coupled classes.

items.title: Drupal 8 deployment and continuous integration
items.full_description:
Until Drupal 7, continuous integration remained challenging for most projects due to architectural limitations. Configuration management emerged as a significant deployment obstacle.

The Configuration Management Initiative in Drupal 8 addresses these issues. This session examines the advantages of implementing CI, reviews practical workflows and available tools, and evaluates how D8 advances deployment and continuous integration capabilities.

items.title: Drupal for Customers: A Shift in Our Thinking
items.full_description:
In the early days of web development, the process seemed straightforward: gather requirements, plan, choose a language, build. However, the proliferation of open source frameworks has complicated this workflow significantly.

The session explores how developers must now navigate licensing discussions, negotiate features with customers, and address questions about module stability and safety. This necessitates rethinking the traditional software design approach.

The talk covers five key areas:

Sell: Understanding how to market Drupal services, differentiate yourself competitively, and communicate open source licensing models to clients.

Plan: Managing evolving project conversations, selecting appropriate modules and libraries, and adapting to constant change.

Build: Working in productive rhythms while providing continuous project feedback.

Scale: Evaluating options within customer contexts and constraints.

Contribute: Helping clients recognise the value of contributing back to maintain long-term project health.

Through interactive discussion, participants will examine each development stage and its implications for developers, site builders, customers, and end users navigating "the fast-moving landscape of Drupal."

items.title: Running Drupal on Microsoft's Azure Cloud Platform
items.full_description:
In this session you will learn the various ways you can host Drupal sites on Microsoft's public cloud platform including deploying from Git/GitHub to Azure Web Sites as well as provisioning a complete Linux web stack to host Drupal on Windows Azure.

The presentation covers building and deploying Drupal on Azure Web Sites with continuous integration from GitHub, configuring automatic scaling for dynamic resource management, provisioning Ubuntu Linux virtual machines through the Azure Portal and CLI tools, utilising pre-built Drupal images from VM Depot, and implementing the Windows Azure Authentication module to enable social logins via Google or Microsoft accounts.
